blocks.content: Structure of a Bank Exam Essay

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: An essay in banking exams follows a three-part structure: Introduction, Body Paragraphs, and Conclusion.
The Introduction should occupy 15–20% of the total word count.
The Body Paragraphs carry the primary content and arguments, making up 60–70% of the essay.
The Conclusion summarizes the discussion and occupies the final 15–20% of the total word limit.

blocks.content: A well-structured essay follows a three-part architecture:

The introduction has one task: capture the reader's attention and clearly state what the essay is about. You can open with a striking fact or statistic ('India processes over 14 billion UPI transactions per month'), a provocative question ('Can a nation of 1.4 billion people achieve universal financial inclusion?'), or a relevant quote. End the introduction with a thesis sentence — a clear statement of your central argument or the scope of your essay.

Each body paragraph should address one main point. Use the P-E-E structure: Point (state the argument), Evidence (support with data or example), Explain (connect back to the topic). For a 300-word essay, aim for 2–3 body paragraphs.

The conclusion should summarise the key insights, state a balanced final judgment, and offer a forward-looking thought. Never introduce new information in the conclusion. Good conclusions connect to the introduction, creating a circular structure.
Descriptive: Explain a concept, scheme, or phenomenon (e.g., 'What is Financial Inclusion?')
Argumentative: Present both sides and take a position (e.g., 'Should bank employees be allowed to strike?')

items: Adhere strictly to the word count distribution: 15–20% for Introduction, 60–70% for Body, and 15–20% for Conclusion.
Avoid allocating too many words to the introduction or conclusion at the expense of main body arguments.

blocks.content: Analytical: Identify causes, effects, and solutions (e.g., 'Causes and Consequences of Rising NPAs')
Contemporary Issues: Comment on current events (e.g., 'India's CBDC — Opportunities and Challenges')

Examiner's Tip: Always connect your essay to banking and finance, even for general topics. An essay on 'Climate Change' should mention green bonds, climate finance, RBI's climate risk framework. This shows that you think like a banker.
